cefoperazone-sulbactam.label: uk3/cefoperazone-sulbactam.json

rows.dose: Maximum 1 g sulbactam every 12 h (2 g/day); extra cefoperazone separately if needed in severe infection
Maximum 500 mg sulbactam every 12 h (1 g/day)

ev: Dosage regimens of SULPERAZON should be adjusted in patients with marked decrease in renal function (creatinine clearance of less than 30 mL/min) to compensate for the reduced clearance of sulbactam

Patients with creatinine clearances between 15 and 30 mL/min should receive a maximum of 1 g of sulbactam administered every 12 hours (maximum daily dosage of 2 g sulbactam), while patients with creatinine clearances of less than 15 mL/min should receive a maximum of 500 mg of sulbactam every 12 hours (maximum daily dosage of 1 g of sulbactam)

rows.dose: Schedule the dose after dialysis (sulbactam is removed by HD); CrCl <15 limits apply

ev: The pharmacokinetic profile of sulbactam is significantly altered by haemodialysis
Thus, dosing should be scheduled to follow a dialysis period

halfLife.ev: After SULPERAZON administration the mean half-life for sulbactam is about 1 hour

renalHalfLife.ev: Patients who are functionally anephric show a significantly longer half-life of sulbactam (mean 6.9 and 9.7 hours in separate studies)

ihd.value: Sulbactam removed by HD; dose after dialysis (label)
ihd.ev: The pharmacokinetic profile of sulbactam is significantly altered by haemodialysis

cefoperazone-sulbactam.summary: Sulbactam limits: CrCl 15–30 → max 1 g sulbactam every 12 h; CrCl <15 → max 500 mg every 12 h. Give after HD.
cefoperazone-sulbactam.sourceNote: Not marketed in the US, UK or EU; renal dosing from the Pfizer SULPERAZON product label (Hong Kong, January 2020). Check the JFDA-approved leaflet for products marketed in Jordan.

roxithromycin.label: uk3/roxithromycin.json

rows.context: Impaired renal function, including renal failure
rows.dose: 300 mg daily (one 300 mg tablet daily, or 150 mg twice daily); no reduction for a normal short course

ev: Impaired renal function Roxithromycin 300 mg tablets: one tablet daily
In the elderly and those with renal failure, dosage reduction is not required for the normally short course of treatment

proteinBinding.ev: Roxithromycin is 92 to 96% bound to plasma proteins (principally alpha-1-acid glycoprotein, but also albumin)

halfLife.ev: The mean half-life of roxithromycin is approximately 12 hours in young adults

renalHalfLife.ev: The half-life is prolonged to 25 hours in patients with impaired hepatic function and 18 hours in patients with renal insufficiency

roxithromycin.kidneyMetric: No renal dose adjustment (NZ data sheet)
roxithromycin.summary: Usual dose in renal impairment; no reduction needed for the normally short course. Half-life ≈18 h in renal insufficiency.
roxithromycin.sourceNote: Not marketed in the US or UK; dosing from the New Zealand Data Sheet (Medsafe, revised 3 November 2025). Check the JFDA-approved leaflet for products marketed in Jordan.

paracetamol.label: uk3/paracetamol.json

rows.dose: Minimum interval 8 hours; use under medical supervision

ev: Where creatinine clearance is between 10-50 ml/min, the minimum interval between administrations should be 6 hours
When creatinine clearance is lower than 10 ml/min, the minimum interval between two administrations should be 8 hours
Paracetamol should be used with caution in the presence of renal insufficiency and increased interval between doses is recommended in cases of severe renal insufficiency

paracetamol.summary: Oral: CrCl 10–50 → at least 6 h between doses; CrCl <10 → at least 8 h. Use with caution in renal insufficiency.
paracetamol.sourceNote: US OTC labels and the UK SmPCs reviewed give no renal dosing interval; intervals from an EU national SmPC (Dutch Medicines Evaluation Board, decentralised procedure DE/H/6508, 25 November 2024). Check the JFDA-approved leaflet for products marketed in Jordan.

diphenoxylate-atropine.label: us3/diphenoxylate-atropine.json

ckd.notes: No renal dose in the label.
ev: Diphenoxylate hydrochloride and atropine sulfate tablets should be used with extreme caution in patients with advanced hepatorenal disease and in all patients with abnormal liver function since hepatic coma may be precipitated

diphenoxylate-atropine.summary: Use with extreme caution in advanced hepatorenal disease (risk of hepatic coma).
